"""Dev-only grader: run course.py's check_N against the stage modules in the
CURRENT working directory — the mutation harness's mutated copies.

    G11_COURSE=<course dir> python3 _build/grade.py [step ...]

Prints the standard block (`✓` pass, `·` todo, `✗` fail) and exits non-zero
unless every requested step passed. `_build/` is excluded from exports, so
this never reaches a learner, and course.py never imports it.
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def _course_dir():
    env = os.environ.get("G11_COURSE")
    if env:
        return os.path.abspath(env)
    probe = HERE
    while True:
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(probe, "course.py")):
            return probe
        parent = os.path.dirname(probe)
        if parent == probe:
            raise SystemExit("set G11_COURSE to the course directory")
        probe = parent


def main(argv):
    work = os.getcwd()
    course = _course_dir()
    os.environ.setdefault("G11_REPO", os.path.dirname(course))
    sys.path.insert(0, work)
    if course not in sys.path:
        sys.path.append(course)
    sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(course))        # codecraft.api
    # Preload every module under test: course.py's own `sys.path.insert(0,
    # HERE)` would otherwise import the pristine course copies instead of the
    # mutated ones the harness planted in `work`.
    import graphs                                    # noqa: F401
    for n in range(1, 11):
        name = "stage_%02d" % n
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(work, name + ".py")):
            __import__(name)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "g11_course", os.path.join(course, "course.py"))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)

    wanted = [int(a) for a in argv if a.isdigit()] or list(range(1, 11))
    ok = True
    for step in wanted:
        fn = getattr(module, "check_%d" % step)
        try:
            fn()
        except NotImplementedError:
            print("· %d. stage_%02d.py not implemented yet" % (step, step))
            ok = False
        except AssertionError as err:
            first = (str(err) or "assertion failed").splitlines()[0]
            print("✗ %d. stage_%02d.py %s" % (step, step, first))
            ok = False
        except Exception as err:                     # noqa: BLE001
            print("✗ %d. stage_%02d.py %s: %s"
                  % (step, step, type(err).__name__, err))
            ok = False
        else:
            print("✓ %d. stage_%02d.py" % (step, step))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Mutation-test this course: plant known bugs in copies of the solutions and
require that the stage's own check catches each one.

    python3 _build/run_mutations.py [_build/mutations.py]

Same contract as `.claude/skills/graded-module/scripts/mutate.py`, but the
checker here is course.py's `check_N` (an authored course has no check.py),
run through `_build/grade.py` in a temporary copy holding the mutated
solutions. A mutant is CAUGHT when the step prints `✗`; a hang is caught.
Exit code 1 if any mutation is MISSED — that means the check is too weak.
"""
import importlib.util
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
COURSE = os.path.dirname(HERE)


def main(argv):
    path = argv[0] if argv else os.path.join(HERE, "mutations.py")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("mutations", path)
    m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    sol = os.path.join(COURSE, "solutions")
    ok = True
    for name, filename, old, new, step in m.MUTATIONS:
        work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mutate-")
        try:
            for f in os.listdir(sol):
                if f.endswith(".py"):
                    shutil.copy(os.path.join(sol, f), work)
            target = os.path.join(work, filename)
            text = open(target).read()
            if old not in text:
                sys.exit("mutation %r: text not found in solutions/%s"
                         % (name, filename))
            open(target, "w").write(text.replace(old, new, 1))
            env = dict(os.environ, G11_COURSE=COURSE)
            try:
                r = subprocess.run(
                    [sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, "grade.py"), str(step)],
                    cwd=work, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
                    env=env)
                caught = "✗" in r.stdout
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                caught = True                    # a hang counts as caught
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
        ok &= caught
        print("%s  step %2s  %s" % ("CAUGHT" if caught else "MISSED",
                                    step, name))
    print("MISSED OR BROKEN: %d" % (0 if ok else 1))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

"""Advanced Data Structures From Scratch — course manifest.

Ten graded stages that build the structures a senior interview still reaches
for, in the order the amortized analysis reaches for them: the binary heap
every sort and scheduler starts from; the d-way heap the same theory
generalises to; the Fibonacci heap in three stages — the O(1) merge, the
consolidation that pays for it, and the cascading cut that makes the deferral
affordable; Dijkstra as the judge all three answer to; the disjoint set whose
counters say whether compression fired; the trie whose autocomplete is why
prefixes exist; the LFU cache whose eviction is one total order; and a
capstone k-d tree that must beat a linear scan by COUNTING its visits, then
audit every bar this course pinned.

The thesis, asserted by every check: THE COUNTER IS THE LESSON. A structure
that returns the right answer can still be the wrong structure — a prune that
never prunes, a sift that rescans, a merge that restructures. Every stage
counts its own work, `graphs.WORK_BARS` holds ceilings measured from the
reference runs, and stage 10 refuses a bar with no measurement behind it.

`graphs.py` is provided and complete: the two graph worlds with their pinned
distance/MST laws, the point world with its brute-force nearest neighbours, the
word list, the fixed LCG, and the bars. Everything is ints; there is no
`random`, no clock, no float anywhere in the graded files.

    python3 codecraft/cli.py run advanced-dsa-from-scratch
"""

from codecraft.api import stage

TITLE = "Advanced Data Structures From Scratch"
DESCRIPTION = ("The heap ladder to the Fibonacci heap and what it is for: "
               "binary and d-way heaps with per-comparison counters, the "
               "lazy merge, consolidation, and cascading cut built one "
               "mechanism per stage, Dijkstra priced on all three heaps, "
               "union-find with counted finds judging Kruskal's MST, the "
               "trie's lexical autocomplete, an LFU cache whose eviction is "
               "one (frequency, age) total order, and a k-d tree verified "
               "against a linear scan by its visit counter — capped by an "
               "audit that fails any work bar left unmeasured.")
LEVEL = "advanced"
ORDER = 42

import os
import sys


def _repo():
    """The repo root: env override, the nearest cwd ancestor holding this
    course, else the two-level default. Nothing below writes a path down."""
    HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    candidates = []
    override = os.environ.get("G11_REPO")
    if override:
        candidates.append(override)
    candidates.append(os.getcwd())
    candidates.append(os.path.dirname(HERE))   # the course sits one level down
    for start in candidates:
        candidate = os.path.abspath(start)
        while True:
            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(candidate,
                                          "advanced-dsa-from-scratch")):
                return candidate
            parent = os.path.dirname(candidate)
            if parent == candidate:
                break
            candidate = parent
    raise SystemExit("cannot find the repo: set "
                     "G11_REPO=/path/to/repo/root")


def _env():
    """Put the course dir first on sys.path and return its imports."""
    HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    if HERE not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
    repo = _repo()
    if repo not in sys.path:
        sys.path.append(repo)
    import graphs
    return graphs


def _refuses(exc, what, call):
    """The one refusal shape: the call must raise `exc`, and the message is
    returned so the check can pin WHICH rule said no."""
    try:
        accepted = call()
    except exc as err:
        return str(err)
    raise AssertionError("%s was accepted: %r" % (what, accepted))

def check_1():

    for i in range(len(heap._a)):

    h.decrease_key(n3, 2)                     # 3 marked, parent 1 marked: cascade
    assert (h.cuts, h.cascades) == (3, 1), (

    assert s5.marked_nodes(h) == (), (

        % (s5.marked_nodes(h),))

        "the cascade destroyed one mark and created two roots: 8 -> 6, got %d"
        % s5.potential(h))
    assert h.is_well_formed()

    # --- refusals name their rule ---------------------------------------------
    _refuses(reject, "a float new key",
             lambda: h.decrease_key(n6, 1.5))

    stranger = other_heap.insert(2)

             lambda: h.decrease_key(stranger, 0))
    _refuses(reject, "a key that is not smaller",
             lambda: h.decrease_key(n6, 9))
    _refuses(reject, "delete of a stranger",
             lambda: h.delete(stranger))

    heap = s5.FibHeap([5, 3, 9, 7])
    target = [x for x in heap.roots() if x.key == 9][0]
    heap.delete(target)
    assert all(x.key != 9 for x in heap._walk()) and heap.n == 3, (
        "delete left the node behind: %r" % ([x.key for x in heap._walk()],))
    assert [heap.pop() for _ in range(3)] == [3, 5, 7]

    # --- the COINS stream: every op, then the bag oracle ----------------------
    for trial in range(2):
        heap = s5.FibHeap()
        bag = []
        handles = {}
        for step in range(240):
            r = graphs.COINS[(trial * 240 + step) % len(graphs.COINS)]
            op = r % 6
            if op < 3 or not bag:
                key = (trial + 1) * 4096 + step
                handles[key] = heap.insert(key, key)
                bag.append(key)
            elif op < 5:
                k = sorted(handles)[r % len(handles)]
                node = handles.pop(k)
                nd = -1 - (trial * 1000 + step)
                heap.decrease_key(node, nd)

                for kk in list(handles):
                    if handles[kk] is node:

            "%s measured %d, ceiling %d — the cut rule is doing work the "
            "amortized argument does not license"

    return "cut rule: cascade pinned 3/1, potential 8->6, 480 stream ops"

"""Advanced Data Structures From Scratch — the graph and point worlds.

The fixtures every stage is judged on: one weighted directed graph with its
pinned single-source distances, the same graph's edges in Kruskal order with
the minimum spanning tree the textbook answer must match, one integer point
set with its brute-force nearest neighbours, the word list the trie answers
from, the LFU script, and the one deterministic byte stream every workload
in the course draws from.

Everything here is ints the whole way — no floats, no `random`, no clock.
The LCG is the only source of "chance" in this course, and it is a constant.
A stage may recompute what it is checked against, but it may never invent a
different answer: when a stage's structure and a brute-force scan disagree,
the scan is law, and `REFERENCE` rows are the scan the course already made.
"""


def _lcg(seed, n):
    """The fixed LCG: the one noise source the world owns."""
    out = []
    state = seed
    for _ in range(n):
        state = (state * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407) & ((1 << 64) - 1)
        out.append((state >> 33) & 0xFF)
    return tuple(out)


#: the deterministic byte stream every graded workload draws from: 4096
#: bytes, one fixed LCG, the same 4096 numbers on every machine.
COINS = _lcg(20261108, 4096)

# --- the weighted directed graph --------------------------------------------------
# Nodes are ints 0..9; an edge is (source, target, weight). The graph is small
# on purpose: every distance, every relaxation count, is checkable by hand.
EDGES = (
    (0, 1, 4), (0, 2, 1), (2, 1, 2), (1, 3, 1), (2, 3, 5), (3, 4, 3),
    (2, 4, 8), (4, 5, 2), (3, 5, 6), (1, 5, 12), (0, 6, 7), (6, 7, 1),
    (7, 8, 5), (8, 9, 3), (6, 9, 14), (4, 7, 2), (5, 9, 1), (2, 6, 3),
    (9, 3, 4), (7, 5, 4),
)

NODES = tuple(sorted({s for s, _t, _w in EDGES} | {t for _s, t, _w in EDGES}))


def adjacency(edges=EDGES):
    """Out-edges per node, in (target, weight) order sorted by target."""
    adj = {node: [] for node in NODES}
    for source, target, weight in edges:
        adj[source].append((target, weight))
    for node in adj:
        adj[node].sort()
    return {node: tuple(rows) for node, rows in adj.items()}


# distances from node 0, computed once here by a plain relax-until-stable scan
# (this fixture never uses a heap; the heaps are what the stages build).
def _brute_distances(source=0):
    adj = adjacency()
    dist = {node: None for node in NODES}
    dist[source] = 0
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for u in NODES:
            if dist[u] is None:
                continue
            for v, w in adj[u]:
                if dist[v] is None or dist[u] + w < dist[v]:
                    dist[v] = dist[u] + w
                    changed = True
    return {node: d for node, d in dist.items() if d is not None}


#: the law for Dijkstra: distances from node 0 over EDGES.
DIJKSTRA_FROM_0 = _brute_distances(0)

# --- the undirected MST world -----------------------------------------------------
UNDIRECTED_EDGES = (
    (0, 1, 4), (0, 2, 1), (1, 2, 2), (1, 3, 5), (2, 3, 8), (2, 4, 10),
    (3, 4, 2), (0, 5, 7), (3, 5, 3), (4, 5, 6), (1, 6, 9), (5, 6, 4),
)

#: Kruskal's own order: (weight, min-endpoint, max-endpoint), ties by nodes.
KRUSKAL_ORDER = tuple(sorted((w, min(u, v), max(u, v))
                             for u, v, w in UNDIRECTED_EDGES))


def _brute_mst():
    """The MST by the slowest obvious method: grow the tree from cheap edges."""
    parent = {u: u for u in range(7)}

    def find(x):
        while parent[x] != x:
            x = parent[x]
        return x

    total = 0
    chosen = []
    for w, u, v in KRUSKAL_ORDER:
        if find(u) != find(v):
            parent[find(u)] = find(v)
            total += w
            chosen.append((u, v, w))
    return total, tuple(chosen)


MST_TOTAL, MST_EDGES = _brute_mst()  # 17, ((0,2,1),(1,2,2),(3,4,2),(3,5,3),(5,6,4),(1,3,5))

# --- the point world for the k-d tree ---------------------------------------------
# integer 2-D points; squared distance is exact in ints, so "nearest" has one
# answer everywhere — and the tree must agree with the linear scan on every
# query, including the ones where two points share a distance.
POINTS = tuple(
    (x, _lcg(1000 + i, 1)[0] % 97)
    for i, x in enumerate(range(0, 48, 2))
) + ((3, 4), (12, 61), (25, 8), (37, 44), (44, 90), (5, 5))


def _brute_nearest(query, k):
    """The linear scan: the law the k-d tree is checked against.

    Order: squared distance, then the point itself, then index. Ties are
    broken by point value, so two implementations can never disagree about
    WHICH tied point answered — only about whether they looked.
    """
    rows = []
    for index, point in enumerate(POINTS):
        d = (point[0] - query[0]) ** 2 + (point[1] - query[1]) ** 2
        rows.append((d, point, index))
    rows.sort()
    return tuple((point, index) for _d, point, index in rows[:k])

NEAREST_3 = tuple(_brute_nearest(q, 3) for q in QUERIES)

"""The k-d tree: split space, prune by the plane, prove it by counting.

La Rocca, ch. 8 — the last structure of the course and the one the whole
syllabus pays for: a binary tree whose levels alternate axes, built by
medians so it is balanced by construction, answering nearest-neighbour
queries by walking down, then deciding with ONE integer comparison whether
the far subtree could possibly hold a closer point. The pruning is the
mechanism; without it the tree is a slow linear scan that stores more.

then by the point, then by index. Squared distances are ints, so there is
no epsilon anywhere. The law has teeth the sloppy implementations miss:
when the split plane's squared gap EQUALS the worst distance in hand, a
point in the far subtree can tie on distance and still WIN on point value
— so the far subtree is pruned only when `gap*gap > worst`, never on `>=`.
The fixture's queries hit this (query (3,3) returns (3,4)@24 then (4,5)@2
then (5,5)@29: all three within a narrow band, ordered by point value on
no tie at all but (7,7)'s 29-vs-29 band is pinned by the scan), so a `>=`
implementation disagrees on a pinned row instead of silently later.

in the tie order by a bisect insert and a truncation: a max-heap of
negated distances gives the same worst bound but loses the ORDERED answer,
and the ORDER is the graded output. k is small (3), so list surgery is the
cheap and the legible thing.

node visits, plane tests, and subtrees skipped. `seen` is what the bar
hangs on: it is the only one that can run away. A prune inverted to
always-descend returns the right rows and pays full linear cost — the
classic "correct but not the structure" bug, invisible to any check that
only reads distances.

"""The tiny API an authored course uses to describe its stages.

A course is a directory containing `course.py`:

    from codecraft.api import stage

    TITLE = "Build a Bloom Filter"
    DESCRIPTION = "A probabilistic set, from hashing to false-positive math."

    def check_1():
        from bloom import BloomFilter
        bf = BloomFilter(bits=64, hashes=2)
        bf.add("x")
        assert "x" in bf
        assert "y" not in bf, "a fresh filter must not report false members"

    STAGES = [
        stage(
            1,
            file="bloom.py",
            title="add and contains",
            tags=["hashing", "data-structure"],
            action="Implement add() to set the k bit positions.",
            predict="can contains() ever be certain an item is absent?",
            hints=["bits = bits[:] to avoid shared state",
                   "use one hash salt per position"],
            check=check_1,
        ),
        ...
    ]

`codecraft run <course>` imports this file, runs each `check`, records the
attempt, and hands the result to the adaptive engine. `hints` are optional —
when omitted, the engine generates them from `action`/`predict`.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional


@dataclass
class Stage:
    id: int
    file: str
    title: str
    check: Callable[[], None]
    tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    action: str = ""
    predict: str = ""
    hints: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    solution: Optional[str] = None   # e.g. "solutions/bloom.py: BloomFilter.add"

    def meta(self) -> Dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "file": self.file,
            "title": self.title,
            "tags": list(self.tags),
            "action": self.action,
            "predict": self.predict,
            "hints": list(self.hints),
            "solution": self.solution,
        }


def stage(id: int, file: str, title: str, check: Callable[[], None],
          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, action: str = "", predict: str = "",
          hints: Optional[List[str]] = None,
          solution: Optional[str] = None) -> Stage:
    """Convenience constructor so course.py stays readable."""
    return Stage(
        id=id, file=file, title=title, check=check, tags=list(tags or []),
        action=action, predict=predict, hints=list(hints or []),
        solution=solution,
    )
